rationale: Stem asks what Freedmen's Bureau reports 'most directly contributed to' — the reports' claims/evidence (southern whites refuse to recognize freedpeople's rights) supported Congress's argument for federal intervention via the Civil Rights Act of 1866 and Congressional Reconstruction. 3.D covers explaining how claims or evidence support an argument. Topic 5.10 Reconstruction is the direct subject; period U5 matches. Note: stem is really a causation question, so the Claims & Evidence parent fits loosely.

Stem asks how the passage's change 'anticipates the ideas behind the' Equal Rights Amendment — explaining how one historical development relates to another (5.B). Topic 7.4 (The Progressives) covers the women's movement/progressive reforms that produced the 19th Amendment and the 1923 ERA proposal. LOW confidence on topic: the stimulus field was empty in the batch file, so the passage itself could not be verified; 7.6 (WWI home front) or 7.8 (1920s cultural controversies) are plausible alternates.

Stem asks what point the 1899 Carson cartoon (Uncle Sam wrestling with the unruly 'Philippines' child) makes — identifying and describing the claim/argument of a non-text-based source (3.A). Topic 7.2 Imperialism: Debates fits the annexation/governance debate over the Philippines better than 7.3 (the war itself).

Stem asks how cars/radios/appliances were sold in the 1920s (installment plans) — identifying the context (buy-now-pay-later credit culture) behind the decade's consumer boom (4.A). Topic 7.7 1920s: Innovations in Communication and Technology covers the consumer economy/installment buying. Flag: this is essentially factual recall, so Developments & Processes (1.A) may be a better parent skill than Contextualization.

Stem asks which historical lesson Reagan's 1983 'simpleminded appeasement' warning recalls — identifying the historical situation of the source (Munich/appeasement lesson, 2.A). Topic 9.3 The End of the Cold War fits Reagan's 1983 anti-Soviet posture; 9.2 Reagan and Conservatism is a possible alternate.

Franklin's 1766 position (aid should 'drive' the poor out of poverty) must be linked to its 'strongest modern echo' (work requirements for welfare) — explaining how one historical development relates to another (5.B). LOW confidence on topic 3.11 (Developing an American Identity): the 1766 quote predates the Revolution and no U3 topic covers colonial poor-relief attitudes directly; 3.11 is the best available as it covers American values/identity.

Stem asks what King's choice of the Lincoln Memorial as setting 'most directly connected his cause to' — identifying the source's purpose (tying civil rights to emancipation, 2.A). Topic 8.10 The African American Civil Rights Movement (1960s) covers the 1963 March on Washington / I Have a Dream.

Stem asks how Salem 'most directly differed from 1950s McCarthyism' — identifying differences/patterns between two historical developments (Salem witch trials vs. Red Scare/McCarthyism, 5.A). Topic 2.7 Colonial Society and Culture covers the Salem witch trials of 1692.
Stem asks which advantage British commanders counted on (command of the sea) — identifying a historical concept/fact of the Revolutionary War (1.A). Topic 3.5 The American Revolution.

EXCEPT question about what early Spanish-Native contact did NOT produce (rapid adoption of horses/cattle) — identifying historical developments/processes of the Columbian Exchange era (1.A). Topic 1.4 Columbian Exchange, Spanish Exploration, and Conquest.

Stem asks which colony was founded as a refuge for English Catholics (Maryland) — identifying a historical fact about colonial founding (1.A). Topic 2.3 The Regions of British Colonies covers the founding/purposes of individual colonies.

Stem asks what change in the southern colonies' slave system began in the 1730s (concentration of enslaved people on large plantations) — identifying a historical development/process (1.A). Topic 2.6 Slavery in the British Colonies.

Stem asks why Dickinson's Letters stopped short of independence (he still hoped for reconciliation within the empire) — explaining the point of view of the source (2.B). Topic 3.3 Taxation Without Representation covers the Townshend-era colonial resistance the Letters responded to.

Stem asks what the Connecticut Plan proposed (bicameral legislature, one house proportional, one equal) — identifying a historical fact about the Constitutional Convention (1.A). Topic 3.8 The Constitutional Convention and Debates over Ratification covers the convention's debates; 3.9 covers the Constitution itself, but the plan was proposed during convention debate.
